facts.text: Colorado Springs was founded as a resort town in 1871 by General William Jackson Palmer after he built the Denver and Rio Grande Railroad.
The city earned the nickname “Olympic City USA” because it hosts the U.S. Olympic & Paralympic Training Center and the national committee headquarters.
Glen Eyrie Castle, built in 1871 for the Palmers, still stands today as a historic landmark overlooking the city.
The Garden of the Gods Visitor & Nature Center on 1805 N 30th St showcases 300‑foot sandstone formations that earned the area National Natural Landmark status.
Colorado Springs’ military presence accounts for more than 40% of the region’s economy, with major defense contractors headquartered there.
The Martin Luther King Jr. Bypass, part of I‑25, runs through the city, reflecting its role in civil rights history.
